title: The US Paid About 2 Cents an Acre for Alaska #shorts
summary: In 1867 the US bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million in gold: about 2 cents an acre of land (our arithmetic from Census and BLM figures).
tags: why did the us buy alaska
sources: Check for the Purchase of Alaska: a $7.2 million check dated August 1, 1868, payable to Russian Minister Edouard de Stoeckl; treaty signed March 30, 1867; the US acquired nearly 600,000 square miles for less than 2 cents an acre; critics called it 'Seward's Folly' (U.S. National Archives, Milestone Documents): https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/check-for-the-purchase-of-alaska

The fur trade in sea otter pelts slumped; the Hudson's Bay Company's economic ambition made the region vulnerable to British designs; after losing the Crimean War to Britain, France, and Turkey in 1856 the tsar was in no mood to see Alaska absorbed by a recent enemy; the tsar set $5 million as the lowest acceptable offer; in 1867 Seward agreed to purchase the territory for $7.2 million; Russia had to wait more than one year to be paid; expansionists saw Alaska as part of the American drive to the Pacific (Library of Congress, Meeting of Frontiers: The Alaska Purchase): https://www.loc.gov/collections/meeting-of-frontiers/articles-and-essays/alaska/the-alaska-purchase/

Total area in square miles: United States (50 states and DC) 3,796,742; Alaska 665,384 (land 570,641); Hawaii 10,932; Texas 268,596; California 163,695; Montana 147,040 (US Census Bureau, State Area Measurements and Internal Point Coordinates, 2010): https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/2010/geo/state-area.html.html
A normal section of land is one square mile, 640 acres (Bureau of Land Management, Land Legal Descriptions): https://or.blm.gov/or/landrecords/legaldescrip.php

Our arithmetic from the sources above: Alaska land area 570,641 sq mi x 640 acres = 365,210,240 acres; $7,200,000 / 365,210,240 acres = 1.97 cents an acre (about 2 cents; the National Archives says less than 2 cents). Lower 48 plus DC total area = 3,796,742 - 665,384 - 10,932 = 3,120,426 sq mi; Alaska's 665,384 is 21.3% of that (about a fifth). Texas + California + Montana = 579,331 sq mi, less than Alaska's 665,384.

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html. The coral treaty lines are drawn approximately from the treaty's wording; the eastern line follows today's boundary.
